title: the gate's installer test can go stale for CLI-source-only changes
description:
internal/release's load-bearing gate test builds ./cmd/ticfac and ./cmd/ticfac-exec-subprocess in subprocesses and asserts on the built binaries' behaviour. Subprocess builds are invisible to go's test cache, and internal/release's import closure does not reach cmd/ticfac/main.go or internal/cli, so a change confined to those sources cannot invalidate the package's cached pass — the gate's installer test can go stale for exactly the changes it most wants to see. install.sh itself is now tracked in-process (this tick); the binaries' source closure is the residual. The full-suite-only harnesses carry the same shape and run cold in CI (reconcile's and herdr's executor builds, cli's built-binary and tk_real tests). Remedy if wanted: -count=1 for internal/release in the gate, or accept with CI's cold full `make test` as the backstop — it runs the installer test on every push.
evidence: internal/release/install_test.go:99
